chunks: And from him, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Muhammad ibn Qays, who said:
I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying, while he was narrating to the people in Mecca, so he said:

"Indeed, a man from the Ansar came to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) asking him, so the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said to him: 'If you wish, ask, and if you wish, I will inform you of what you came to ask me about.' He said: 'Inform me, O Messenger of Allah.'

He said: 'You came to ask me about your reward in your Hajj and Umrah. Indeed, for you, when you set out for the path of Hajj, then mounted your mount, then said "Bismillah" and "Alhamdulillah", then your mount proceeded, placing no hoof and raising no hoof, except that a good deed was recorded for you and a bad deed was erased from you.
When you entered the state of Ihram and responded (with Talbiyah), for every Talbiyah you recited, you have ten good deeds recorded, and ten bad deeds erased from you.
When you circumambulated the Sacred House seven times, that is a pledge and treasure with Allah, which He is shy to punish you after it forever.
When you prayed two rak'ahs behind the Maqam, for them there are for you a thousand accepted Hajjs.
When you walked between As-Safa and Al-Marwah, for you is like the reward of one who performed Hajj on foot from his country, and like the reward of one who freed seventy believing slaves.
When you stood at Arafat until sunset, if upon you are sins like the sand of 'Araj, or like the number of stars in the sky, or like the drops of rain, Allah will forgive them for you.
When you threw the pebbles at the Jamarat, for every pebble, ten good deeds are recorded for you in what remains of your life.
When you shaved your head, for the count of every hair, a good deed is recorded for you in what remains of your life.
When you slaughtered your offering or sacrificed your camel, for every drop of its blood, a good deed is recorded for you in what remains of your life.

When you visited the House, circumambulated it seven times, and prayed two rak'ahs behind the Maqam, an angel struck your shoulders and said to you: 'Allah has forgiven you what passed, and for what is between you and one hundred and twenty days.'

key_terms.إِحْرَام: The state of consecration for pilgrimage
key_terms.رَمْي الْجِمَار: Throwing pebbles at the pillars in Mina
key_terms.هَدْي: The sacrificial animal offered during Hajj

ai.seo_question: What are the specific spiritual rewards for each ritual of Hajj according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the Shia emphasis on the cumulative merit of ritual precision, where each physical act of Hajj—from the journey to the sacrifice—is quantified with specific spiritual rewards. It underscores the concept of divine generosity (*karam*) in erasing sins, culminating in a promise of forgiveness for the past and the subsequent 120 days, reflecting the belief in the transformative power of sincere pilgrimage.
